$comment: Each entry is a MINIMUM number of tests that project must actually run and
pass. Adding specs raises the real count and never fails this file; lowering
a number here, or deleting tests until the real count falls below one, is the
event this file exists to make visible.
It was 1 and 1, which made the green line 'coverage floor: OK (desktop=9
mobile=9)' a REPORT of what ran rather than a floor that was enforced. An
independent verifier showed that `--grep "reports liveness"` then exited 0
with one test per project. Wholesale vacuity was caught; attrition was not.
JSON, not TypeScript, because two very different readers need the same
Playwright process) and scripts/ci/check-coverage-floor-ran.mjs (the CI step
that re-checks the finished run from outside it). A number duplicated in two
files is a number that drifts.
RAISING THESE IS PART OF EACH UI PR. A slice that adds specs raises its
project's minimum in the same diff, so the ratchet only ever goes up.
